properties.inspection_comments: Purpose: To conduct a food safety inspection in accordance with WAC Chapter 246-215. During this food safety inspection, 100 or more red high risk points were cited. This is your second inspection with 100+ red points. An educational visit is now required. All employees must be present at the educational visit. You will be billed $240 per hour to include inspector travel time for this visit. Please contact the inspector listed at the bottom of this report to set-up a time. The educational visit will focus on serving safe food and successfully passing future inspections. A third party interpreter will be provided if necessary . Additional inspections with 100 or more red points will result in closure of your business. Here is an overview of the process if 100 or more red points are cited during future inspections: 3rd inspection with 100 or more red points: • Facility is closed for 24 hours. • Charged pre-opening inspection ($360). • Informal administrative conference at Tacoma -Pierce County Health Department. • Create risk control plan with inspector. • Charged follow-up inspection ($240). 4th inspection with 100 or more red points: • Facility is closed for 24 hours. • Charged pre-opening inspection ($360). • Formal administrative conference ($840). • Probation for 6 months: -5 additional inspections ($480 each). -Facility is closed each time a probation violation is cited. Due to 35 or more red points, a follow-up inspection will be conducted for the red item violations noted in this inspection report. A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required. Notes: - Keep chlorine sanitizer between 50-200 pmm. Mix 1 tsp bleach per gallon of water. - Observed fryer line dripping into a bucket. Repair fryer to not drip. All equipment must be maintained in good repair. Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 06/11/2026 1800 Proper cooking time and temperature; proper use of noncontinuous cooking. 1800 Observed pork that was in the grill drawers. PIC stated that the pork is cooked overnight when no employees are present. I asked to see the data log or the logs taken for the pork, and they did not have any. Per your prep steps a Elitech GSP-6 continuous temperature monitoring unit would be inserted into the pork roast before being placed in the oven at 300F. Per PIC they had a data logger, but it broke and they have not obtained a new one. Per your approval letter, You are approved with unattended cooking procedures for pork shoulder (roast). You must follow the written procedures for this process as approved. If found operating without the required equipment (continuous temperature data logger) or without maintaining data logged information, approval for this process will be revoked. You must maintain data logs for this process on site and have them available for review during inspections. Stop overnight cooking immediately. Facility is not approved to overnight cook until they provide inspector proof of a functional data logger. Ensure that logs are being taken for the overnight cooking or this process will be revoked and all of the pork cooked overnight will be discarded. * A compliance order has been issued to immediately stop overnight cooking until you provide inspector proof of a functional data logger. Failure to stop overnight cooking until you provide inspector proof of a functional data logger will result in a fee of $240 for non-compliance. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items. properties.inspection_comments: Purpose: To conduct a food safety inspection in accordance with WAC Chapter 246-215. Due to 35 or more red points, a follow-up inspection will be conducted for the red item violations noted in this inspection report. A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required. Notes: - Be sure sinks are being used for designated purposes only: handwash sinks are for handwashing only, prep sinks for food prep only. -Ensure to limit time that TCS food is left out to keep it out of the temperature danger zone . - Do not stock above fill lines in prep top coolers. - Make sure all cold held time/temperature control for safety(TCS) food held for longer than 24 hours is being properly date marked with date opened or prepped and are being discarded by the 7th day or manufacturer's best-by date, whichever comes first. -TCS food thawed from frozen must have updated date mark upon removal from freezer. If food is frozen same day it is prepped, mark food with discard time 6 days from thaw date once removed from freezer. Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 06/10/2026 2600 Compliance with valid permit; operating and risk control plans and required written procedures. 2600 Observed in walk-in cooler whole uncut beef prime rib and individually portioned prime rib. Per employee, beef was cooked yesterday and stated it is cooked to 100F, moved to cool whole in the walk-in cooler, then cut and portioned, cooked on grill to order. Rib can be ordered mid-rare/undercooked per customer order. Observations and process described during today's inspection do not comply with cooking, cooling, or undercooking service standards in WAC 246-215 03400(2)a regarding whole meat roasts. All processes must be written and approved by the health department and follow food safety standards as established . Instructed facility to discard prime rib and portioned rib for safety. A compliance order has been issued to stop preparation of prime rib immediately . Failure to stop preparation of prime rib immediately will result in a $240 non-compliance fee. Facility must provide food preparation steps for prime rib roast that comply with the cooking, cooling, or undercooking service standards for review to food@tpchd.org or to inspector at dcaverly@tpchd.org. Prime rib educational handout provided in inspection report email. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items.
